items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: We weren’t playing Patti Page’s “Love” or whatever, “Love Love Love.” ... Patti Page — I played the bass on that show.

ctx.x: Okay. So do you remember what kind of music, some of the songs you would have played at your first wedding gig?

Well I mean it would have been “It Had to be You,” — oh what were the songs — “Poor Butterfly.” Of the songs — the standards of 1956. I mean we weren’t playing Patti Page’s “Love” or whatever, “Love Love Love.” We weren’t doing that kind of stuff. We were doing “Someday Sweetheart,” “Charmaine,” “I Found a New Baby.” Things like that. But usually at weddings you couldn’t really unload because dancers, you know, they’ve got to do the — now I’ve got to play a waltz, for the wedding waltz or whatever it was, things…
That’s okay. Hey you don’t have to like everything. Well it seems like you must have been getting to a point where you decided well this is what I’m going to do.
